doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Making Spring Garden: a quartet with its own personality
summary: He did not try to play the score literally, leaving room for Rich Perry and improvisation.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: “Why is it going like that when I walk?” Oh that’s really good. Well I have a couple of comments about the recording, which I really liked, which I think can stand by itself as a recording or you can listen to it with “The Rite of Spring” in mind. And I wonder did you have that in mind or were you really trying to reflect Stravinsky as close as you could?

No the thing, I realize with the quartet, especially we had a little rehearsal in Argentina, we got a chance to play again together. We hadn’t played for some years. And I realized that it was going to have a personality of its own. And it wasn’t like I could assign these guys, okay we’re all going to listen to “The Rite of Spring” and then you come in with all the licks you can, we’re going to just do this. It wasn’t that, and I knew my fingers aren’t on all the notes there, I’m just trying to grab things sometimes to refer to Stravinsky, so that’s the way I wrote it for them. I wanted them to be who they are and with Rich Perry, Rich Perry is going to be Rich Perry and we hired him because of his great sound and you’re going to know it’s him, regardless of the music. So especially after we had our little rehearsal I just said this is going to go the way it’s going to go and I’m just going to try to give some suggestions which we did. And then we left out some things. There were just some things that when we rehearsed on the day of the recording just like okay that

ain’t going to work, okay. And we needed to leave room for improvisation so it wasn’t like I was going to be literal and try to play the whole score. And then there’s just things like you know even that thing [bangs piano] there was no way I was going to play that exactly because I mean it could be played, and I know it, but I spaced it out in some way, just like gave a suggestion. So basically the comments from people I really respect have been very very good, I’m very pleased, because I think they got my idea and the fact that you know I wasn’t going to just try to play the score.
